rules.rule: Check for same-day referral after a seizure/fit
rules.problem: Check task mixes in faint features (collapse, twitching, flushing, dizziness, nausea, sweating) from the 'No' branch, and diabetes/glucose context; acceptable only to satisfy the checked-for rule for the faint diagnosis, but does not itself correspond to a page box

rules.rule: Diagnose probable meningitis after a seizure/fit
rules.problem: Any-of structure (temp, headache, neck stiffness, rash) follows page wording literally but headache alone yields 'probable meningitis'; page grammar is ambiguous

rules.rule: Diagnose probable stroke from focal signs (seizure/fit page)
rules.problem: Page's 'No' branch (not a seizure); rule has no seizure-absent condition and drops 'new sudden' on speech/visual items

rules.rule: Diagnose probable TIA from focal signs (seizure/fit page)
rules.problem: Same as stroke: identical criteria, no way to distinguish; page gives 'Stroke or TIA likely' as one box so acceptable, but no seizure-absent condition
Drops 'lasting < 15 seconds' and 'rapid recovery'; weaker than page, likely over-triggers

rules.rule: Urgent: same-day referral after a seizure/fit
rules.problem: Omits 'glucose unable to measure' and malaria-area positive test items; faithful otherwise; Urgent level matches 'Refer same day'

summary: Most consequential: the page's 'If patient had >= 2 definite seizures with no identifiable cause, doctor to consider epilepsy' (and the known-epilepsy routine-care branch) is not encoded, so no possible Epilepsy diagnosis exists; also the common-faint rule drops the <15 second duration and rapid recovery, and glucose 'unable to measure' is missing from the Urgent rule. Otherwise every condition traces to the page with correct roles, thresholds and time directions, and all SNOMED concepts exist.
